The final answer 77 is incorrect, because the proposed solution misstates Looijenga's theorem.

**The cited theorem is misapplied.** Looijenga's results on \(R^*(\mathcal M_g)\) are:
- \(R^d(\mathcal M_g)=0\) for \(d>g-2\), and \(R^{g-2}(\mathcal M_g)\cong\mathbb Q\).
- Faber's results show the kappa monomials of degree \(d\) are linearly independent for \(d\le \lfloor g/3\rfloor\). This is the relation-free range, and it is not the range \(g>2d\).

The condition \(g>2d\) does not guarantee the absence of relations in degree \(d\).

**Why 77 cannot be right.** For \(g=25\), \(\lfloor g/3\rfloor=8\). Faber showed \(R^*(\mathcal M_g)\) is generated by \(\kappa_1,\dots,\kappa_{\lfloor g/3\rfloor}\). So \(R^{12}\) is spanned by monomials in \(\kappa_1,\dots,\kappa_8\) of degree 12. The number of partitions of 12 with all parts \(\le 8\) is \(p(12)-7=70\), since the 7 partitions with a part \(\ge 9\) are excluded. Thus \(\dim R^{12}(\mathcal M_{25})\le 70<77\).

The proposed value \(77=p(12)\) would require no relations among the degree-12 kappa monomials, which contradicts this bound. The exact value needs Faber's conjectural/known structure of \(R^*(\mathcal M_{25})\), which the proposed solution does not use.

VERDICT: REJECT
